title: Skip-the-Line Group Tour of the Vatican, Sistine Chapel & St. Peter's Basilica
description: Make the most of your valuable vacation time by skipping the line at the Vatican Museums. You save hours waiting by booking a group tour, and get engaging commentary from your guide as you explore. Admission is included to the Sistine Chapel and St. Peter's Basilica; follow your guide on a carefully-crafted itinerary to ensure you don't miss a thing.

reviews.usertext:
We booked this tour directly on the Made in Rome Tours website, for myself and my mother (Trip Advisor doesn't have an option for an adult family group so I chose solo) who had just turned 70, to avoid the long lines. It turns out we not only got that, but also had a great guide with Lucia.

August is a very busy month there, so they had 8 groups leaving at the same time, and half of them would start at St Peters, instead of finishing there like the itinerary says, to offset the amount of people. We were in one of those groups with Marco, but I talked to him saying that we'd prefer to finish at the Basilica so we could climb to the top after the tour. Marco quickly called the office and arranged for us to move to Lucia's group, that would do the original itinerary we were looking for. It all worked smoothly and we really appreciated that.

Lucia was great! She's very knowledgeable, and offered a lot of information, and with a critical commentary too. I like that and we could tell she knew a lot in relation to the subject. It was a dream seeing the Sistine Chapel and St Peters Basilica, as well as a selection of important works from the extensive Vatican Museums. One day I'll go back to spend a full day there on my own time, but if you have limited time like we did, this is an amazing option.

Thank you Lucia for your friendliness, your kindness and all your knowledge!
- Carlos & Angela

A brilliant tour seeing one of the holiest places on earth! Giuliano was our excellent English speaking tour guide who was clear and easy to understand. He guided us through all the security checks into the Vatican with ease. The audio guides were very helpful even if some needed replacing but that is due to the Vatican not updating the guides since 2005 to a more modern digital version but we all managed. The sights we saw are truly amazing and it’s quite a privilege to actually stand where so many popes and dignitaries have stood before in such beautiful surroundings steeped in history. There was so much to see and learn about that you end up with brain overload. The Sistine chapel was awesome. It doesn’t disappoint. How Michelangelo managed to paint all that in 9 years in total during his lifetime is inspiring. We were also lucky enough to see St Peter’s Basilica which re-opened after Covid closures. So many photo opportunities. Truly magnificent. The Vatican museum is very big and we weren’t able to stop and look at everything as there wasn’t enough time on the actual tour, however, once the tour is over, you are free to go and look at it again in more detail but to be honest, after nearly four hours of walking about in 35c heat, all you really want to do is sit down and eat and drink something which you can do inside the museum or sit outside in its gardens. I’d recommend revisiting in a cooler month and buying an solo entry ticket to the museum just to be able to take your time at your own pace to really be able to study everything and see all the artefacts. In the meantime this tour was well worth it and I’d highly recommend it. Enjoy! 😊

Highly recommend booking the "Skip-the-line" tour as by 9am there was already an extremely long queue to enter the Vatican City Museums.

Incredible to walk through the rooms and see the sculptures and paintings. The Sistine Chapel was amazing although a lot smaller than I anticipated.

I give this 4/5 for the reason, I didn't find the tour guide as good as the others I had listened too throughout my stay in Rome.

I accept that the Vatican is very busy right now but this does mean that a decent guided tour with 30 people on it is almost impossible to do. The information given as we waited to enter St. Peter’s and inside the grounds before the Sistine Chapel was interesting and useful because it was delivered in a calm way. However it was difficult to take anything else in because the guide just kept walking ahead and narrating what he could see which was rarely what we could see because he was usually 5-15 metres ahead. If you paused to actually look at anything he was talking about you lost him & had to push through crowds to catch up. The guide asked if there were questions but was impatient with those who asked so it was a 3 hour monologue. I got the impression he didn’t really like his job. I booked this tour because the Vatican website was so hard to penetrate but on reflection I’d try harder with the website and save the money. We would have got more out of reading a guide book and the one line we skipped (the museum queue) was actually really short.

This tour was a mess from the start. At least 10 separate groups of people waiting outside the office just wondering what's going on. Our group was scheduled for 8:45AM but didn't get assembled until 9AM where we immediately rushed to get in line for the security. Thankful that we rushed since the "skip the line" feature does not exist here and did save some time getting there sooner (if only we had left at 8:45 when we were supposed to).

Guide went first through security and he did not do much of waiting around for the group to get through. Relying on a headset and hoping to find him in a large crowd of people, so no surprise when you nearly lose part of the group along the way. The basilica portion of the tour went ok as there was more space and ease of getting around due to a smaller crowd, but there was little direction from the guide other than "follow me". The only information he provided was to look at the detail and compare the size of the artwork to various things, something any person could understand without any help. I was hoping this would improve as the tour went on but things only got worse. The vatican museum was him just running through telling us to keep up while the rooms/hallways packed with frescas and sculptures were rarely described. It was hard to even glance at half of the things in the museum without feeling belittled and yelled at to keep up.

This tour needs more time to be worthwhile in general. However, our guide also was not very informative which made for a bad combination. We even passed some other groups where I actually removed my headset to listen to them describe some of the sculptures and why they were assembled in the room the way they were. I learned more in a few minutes from a separate group than in 3hrs with the guide I had!

Overall, this tour was very disappointing and is way overpriced given that the museum ticket is the only thing that costs money (roughly 17 euros). Do yourself a favor and do not book with this touring company. Go by yourself or find a separate guide for the places individually to get your money's worth instead. The 3hrs to encompass all of the places mentioned is not enough time even with a really good guide. The Basilica and Vatican museums are beautiful places and it's a shame that they get whisked over by these groups without describing it's beauty.

Note: I don't remember my guide's name but I included a picture of him below. He's holding the red flag and that was exactly what he was for this tour, a walking red flag. Avoid at all costs!

One of the worst tours we have been on by far; to pay nearly $150 for this tour for 2 people is ridiculous. Too rushed with a guide that seemed uninterested. We got to the meeting location at 8:20 am on October 29 and by 8:40 the company commenced separating us into groups, and we were placed in group 16 with 10 people total at 9 am. From there we walked to the Vatican which is about 1/2 to 3/4 of a mile. Tour commenced inside the Vatican at 9:40 am and ended in less than 2 hours. The tour guide told us the tour would be 3 hours! Why is this a big deal? We felt rushed the entire time, and the guide was moving us quickly from place to place while talking to us. She wasn’t engaging and it just felt like she wanted to this tour to be done sooner rather than later. This was in contrast to other groups we saw where the guides were taking their time, stopping at displays and explaining in detail what they were viewing. We got information that felt like it was a Wikipedia paragraph. Had high hopes for this given the reviews on Trip advisor but it was a major disappointment. Can’t recommend this tour. On a side note, we explored on our own including climbing St. Peter’s Basilica which offers amazing views and 1,102 steps.

We loved this tour and our guide Marco really made the experience. The Vatican museums and the Sistine Chapel were very busy but having a guide who was knowledgable and engaging helped make the most of it and our boys engaged. With queues for the Basilica up to 3 hours in the square and only a few days to explore Rome it was well worth the price and made the most of our time. 100% recommend

The skip the line tour was recommended to us and it did not disappoint. Our guide Lucia was very knowledgeable about St Peters Basilica and the art and sculptures contained in it. Lucia also had great information about the works in the various rooms in the vatican museums.
Best tip we got was pay for the elevator if you are going to the top of the dome of the basilica! It is €10 and means that you only need to climb 330 stairs instead of nearly 900. The climb is not for the faint hearted however the view at the top is absolutely spectacular.
One thing to be aware of is that during the tour when you leave St Peters Basilica, if you want to return to wander through the amazing church again you will have to queue to go through the security barrier again. We did this and although the queue looked large, we only had to wait about ten minutes. Definitely worth it although I'm not sure it would be that quick at the peak of summer tourist season.
I would definitely recommend this tour, it was enjoyable and added to the experience.

The tour was supposedly for 3h.
40mins at the beginning at their office to hear the history of the Sistine Chapel.
20mins at St Peter's Square & history about it
15 mins at Piazza San Pietro
45 mins at Vatican Museum
15 mins at Sistine chapel
15 mins at St Peter's Church
We were in a small group of 10. Most of the time was spent walking & waiting.
We were whisked through the Vatican Museum in 5-10 minutes, no stop was made or stories given. All we heard was "I am walking" from the guide as she guided us through the museum to get to the chapel.
We were left before reaching the Sistine chapel and asked to return our headsets.
Gratuities handed over and goodbyes said.
Please don't join the tour, you are better off just buying the Skip-The-Line tickets & make use of the free audio sets that are available at each point.

I had a great experience with this tour. While it can be overwhelming to be in a tour going through such a busy place, our tour guide Marco made it feel very personal and fun. While Marco himself said that he loves to talk about dates, he did it in a way that was both informative and easy to understand. It was also obvious how much passion Marco had for his job. As a teacher myself, I was also impressed by how engaging the tour was for the children who joined us. We definitely skipped a long line of people both at the Vatican Museum line and the Saint Peter's Basilica, that alone made it worth the cost. It was also great to have a guide explain some of the art as you see it, so you can focus on the art and not the written text beside it (or sometimes not beside it). I would definitely recommend this tour!

Excellent tour. Well worth the money just to be guided through all the queues and security and not try and navigate that minefield in extremely hot temperatures. The headsets provided throughout the tour was fantastic as you could always hear the guide even if you were at the back or lingering a moment or two longer at a painting. Highly recommend this tour. All very well organised and the guide was very knowledgeable and happily answered any questions people had. The guide also very considerate about the sun/heat and kept to shade where possible and informed when we were approaching water fountains and also told parents with strollers where and when they could be used or not or if could be carried.

Marco our guide was very knowledgable about Rome in general was also very friendly. He looked after us all very well. The queue outside the Vatican Museum for those who didn’t have pre booked tickets (like we did) was worth the money we paid

We took this tour (signed up about a month in advance) on Oct. 4. It was well worth the money we paid. The lines were exceeddingly long at all points on the tour, so our ability to "Skip the Line" was essentialk to being able to see everything.
We had a really exceptional Tour Guide in "Solomon" (her last name). She knew the site, handled her group in the crowded conditions very well, and you could tell she loved sharing the Vatican, Sistine Chapel, and St. Peter's with us. She did not seem to be a native English speaker, but she was easy to understand, and I have trouble hearing! But she was clear and spoke slowly enough to easily comprehend what she was saying. We used the "earpieces" which were essential in the very crowded conditions and the noise that created. thank you for such a professional operation.

Well organised tour. Informative guide who was relaxed and friendly. Visiting the Vatican is chaotic and confusing, so we decided to pay for this tour (normally would organise it ourselves). It was worth the extra expense. There is sooooo much to see at the Vatican museums and we would have been overwhelmed without our guide. The group was small (about 10-12 people) and there was no faffing. We left the tour just before the Sistine Chapel so we could look at the Rafael rooms which took us an extra hour or so, before finishing with the Sistine. The guide sorts all the tickets out and it was a relief to just sit and wait for a while whilst he dealt with the crazy crowds at the ticket desk. I am giving 5 stars as it really suited us. We spent about 4-5 hours in total on the tour which was definitely enough for us. If you want to spend longer in the Vatican museum I would select a different tour… there were people doing a much more detailed study of the art works in other groups.

Would I recommend this tour? Perhaps but truly not sure how to rate it as I was disappointed for many reasons.
We were on time and Marco was our Guide, he was polit and nice but mostly had conversation with the younger couple from California as he had some interest in California and been there so rest of us basically just were following him quietly with no interaction with him for the first 20/30 minutes.
Skip-The-Line MMMM I would not say is completely true as we had to line up to go Inside (Vatican)
Just like everyone else who was in line so there was no privilege given there.
Marco was very Knowledgeable but for lack of better words he was very distracted, Group was all over the place and he would just walk away with out paying attention if we are following him or even did we all see him changing direction and do believe me the flag that he was holding up gets lost in that crowed. There was time that we had to run to get back to the group and yet he had no Idea we were falling behind due to the cowed blocking us from getting through.
He only gave 5 Minutes washroom break when he was getting entry ticket for Sistine Chapel and as we all know how lady’s bathroom all mostly crowed so there goes that idea.
He also did not accompany us for Sistine chapel as he said is useless to continue the with the tour as he cannot talk when we are going through the chapel, Truly the quiet part of the tour is actually only a few minutes but he insisted that we go on our own as he wanted to go back and return the radios… which again was another disappointment so really should I recommend this Tour? We did learn a lot and I thank him for that.

This company oversold their tours for the day we took this tour. There were 10 groups of customers, and we had 30 people in our tour group. That was too many people per tour group. The company should have limited the number of people per group to 15 like other tour companies in Rome do. Also, everyone was asked to meet at the same time, at a very small office on a very small street in Vatican City. The street was crowded with tourists when the company could have easily scheduled their tours throughout the morning to lessen the crowd. Finally, the Whisper equipment we had to use was inadequate, as the design required a very small plastic loop hold a speaker against your ear while you walked. It did not stay on for me or most of the group. Better equipment that will stay on should be used. We really liked our guide, and he did give a god tour. But, much of his time was spent managing our large group, and it was obvious that it was a struggle to keep us all together and close enough to hear him. e would not recommend this tour company.

Excellent tour! My husband and I visited on 2nd May 2022. Marco (our guide) was very knowledgeable on the Vatican and made the trip enjoyable for all. Firstly we visited the basilica, where we were told about the history as well as various statues and artworks. We then headed to the Vatican museums and the sistine Chapel where we learned more about the various pieces on display and more detail on Michaelangelo's famous fresco painting of the ceiling. The tour didn't include going under the Basilica and viewing the cypts of the popes, which would have been great - but access to St. Peter's is free, so you could go back again after visiting the museums and view this yourself. All round fab tour, would definitely recommend for couples, solo visiters and families alike.

This was the first tour we did during our time in Rome, and it got our trip off to an amazing start. Everything about this tour was easy, from finding the meeting point, to entering the sites. Everything was organised for us, and it meant we got to simply enjoy it. We had Lucia as our guide, and we couldn't fault her in any way. She was friendly, even taking the time to go round the group and ask everyone their name and where they were from. Lucia clearly has lots of knowledge which she was able to communicate effectively to the group. Out of the 2 of us that took this tour, 1 of us had previously visited Rome and the attractions on this tour, while the other hadn't. However, we both were able to learn lots, with Lucia pointing out very intricate details which I had not previously been shown. She was able to do this without boring us or overloading us with information. She also gave us lots of opportunities for photos, and explained everything as she did it. Even showing us how we would return to the sites, and where to go from the ending point. Lucia was able to give information about Rome in general too, even offering restaurant recommendations to a member of the group. She kept a good pace, and allowed us to enjoy our time in Rome. This tour is also great value for money, with it being the only one I could find which includes St Peter's Basilica alongside the Vatican Museums. I would recommend this tour to anyone, and I would definitely book this again should I return to Rome.

Early ish start, great guide who explained the tour before we left, always kept the group together ensured everyone was gathered at the most important aspects of the tour. Ear phones are essential especially in the Vatican museum and way into Sistine Chapel. 3 hours packed full of history, well worth the price of the ticket

We took the St. Peter, Vatican Museum and Sistine Chappel tour early in the AM during the month of July.
Our tour guide Simona was very knowledgeable and considerate. She pointed out all important points as well as areas to rest and refill water bottles. Our tour was about 3 h in length and we were able to visit on our own after the tour was over. Our tour departed from the meeting point at 8:45 Am and we were surprised how busy it was at that time already. We spent a good amount of time in St. Peter Basilica but the Vatican Museum portion was more of a walk with pointers than the stop and look type tour. The Sistine chapel portion was done on our own but Simona pointed out many things to look for in advance.

Robert was our guide - This was a great tour!! Some of the reviews don’t understand that you can’t skip the security line, you only skip the line to get into Vatican Museums and Sistine Chapel. We booked Friday morning 8.45 tour. Get yourself there early, approx 8:00-8:15 to get yourself into the first group, then go get a coffee & pastry while you wait. We only queued about 30 minutes for security checks to get into St Peters Basilica, the line moves really quickly! We were straight into the Vatican museums, just a short wait for security. All was absolutely fine!! Be prepared to be pushed a little as it is VERY busy and small corridors. It is 100% worth the money on this, I have walked away knowing so much history and fact nuggets than I would just taking myself around. When you walk passed the Vatican museums queue, you will see how worth it this is! Thank you SO much Robert!

Booked this for the 12th April. We arrived at the meeting point early, and then went and grabbed a coffee. We’d recommend this as you do find that a lot of people arrive in a narrow street, with taxi’s dropping people off. Our guide, Marco, got us started right on time. Can’t fault him he was engaging and exceptionally well informed. We couldn’t skip the line due to current COVID restrictions, no one could. Although I think the Vatican opened the access up about an hour after our tour started! Be prepared for it to be heaving with tourists. It can become difficult to move in the Vatican museums and you do rush through these areas. However the tour was very good, well worth it and Marco was brilliant. We would definitely recommend this tour.

Excellent Experience with Tour Guide Filippo and Made in Rome Tours, Skip The Line Tour of Vatican Museum and St. Peter's ! Filippo was a most knowledgeable tour guide and did a great job of explaining and relating the Vatican art and traditions to American Culture, with entertaining facts and humor. Filippo's English skills are excellent. We were a group of 4 people in our 60s and 70s. The tour was well-paced and Filippo was continuously mindful of our comfort and to focus on the interests and questions from our small tour group. I highly recommend this tour group for their quality and value of price. Thank you!

Our tour guide Bob took us calmly through what would have been a chaotic visit without him. Having the knowledge of the queuing and entry systems ensured that we got smoothly into each of the attractions without any problems.
We were very pleased to have booked in advance as turning up on the day doesn’t necessarily mean tickets are available.
Bob had excellent and interesting knowledge of St Peter’s Basilica, The Vatican Museums and Yge Sistine Chapel and his stories and facts were a pleasure to listen to.
I would absolutely recommend this tour with this company.

We booked this tour a month ahead because it consistently garnered great reviews. And it again deserves a perfect 5 from us! Grazie mille to Lucia our guide. Very knowledgeable, friendly, thorough and professional - she really took extra care of all of us making sure no one was left behind like a mother hen! You won't get it wrong in choosing this tour!

Gabriel gave my college group an excellent tour of St. Peter's, the Sistine Chapel, and even the museum rooms, and was very knowledgeable on all the questions we asked him. The headsets were very helpful, although they can flake out if the guide gets into the next room well ahead of you. (And of course security-checkpoint lines are not possible to be skipped, along with general delays from crowds or a cardinal's funeral.)

Despite booking the earliest time slot available, with skip the line access, this tour was so crowded it was not very enjoyable.

Our tour guide was good, but couldn't make up for the rushed nature of the tour. Our time in St Pater's Basilica was the highlight. We had about 45 minutes of time to explore on our own, and a mass was in progress at the time so it made for a good experience. It is really just a gorgeous church, massive in size, and ornate in detail. I could easily spend hour in there exploring all the nooks and crannies, all the frescoes, sculptures, mosaics, reliefs, architecture, etc. It is awe-inspiring whether you are religious or not.

Moving on to the Vatican Museums and Sistine Chapel is where this tour stumbled. Both were so overcrowded as to prevent any meaningful time to appreciate any of the works. We just walked straight through the halls without really stopping at any of the works along the way. It felt like a race to the Sistine Chapel.

Once in the Sistine Chapel, the guards inside moved people through like herding cattle, not allowing people to stop and take in the splendor of Michelangelo's masterpiece ceiling frescoes.

Sure, we can says we were there, but that doesn't mean much is you don't get to stop and enjoy the views.

Even mid morning the queue to get into the Vatican City is huge, so beating these queues saves a huge amount of time. Starting in the square the tour proceeded through the magnificent St.Peters then onto the museum a few minutes walk away. So much to see here that you only get a taste. The tour exits through the Sistine Chapel. Plenty of good information from our guide via headphones. Highly recommended.

The tour of the Vatican, Sistine Chapel and St Peters Basilica was very good. Skipping the line is a no-brainer! Our guide was extremely knowledable, animated and clearly very passionate about the history of these religious sites.
The only downside was the tour felt very rushed and we only had 10 mins to see the Sistine Chapel.

Our “group” was small (around 20 people) but there were 10 groups leaving for the 9am tour. Because of this, half the groups went to St Peters first which required an hour long wait in line for security. After St Peters, we exited and walked to the Vatican Museum entrance where we had to go through security again!

The groups that went to the Vatican Museum first avoided the long line for St Peters since you can enter the Sistine Chapel and St. Peters directly from the Museum.

I get that everyone is trying to make up for lost revenue following the pandemic but increasing the number of groups leaving at one time is impacting the quantity of this tour experience.

My recommendation if choosing this tour is to request that you be included in a group that is going to the Vatican Museum first. Otherwise you’ll finish around 3pm and stand in long lines.

The good: the guide was friendly, positive, spoke good english and was knowledgeable.

The “so-so”: the group was 30 people (larger than advertised) and we spent a long time waiting around. I do not understand why this tour company needs to queue to rent head sets at the Vatican museum and then again at the basilica when other companies e.g at the colosseum have their own head sets which you get at the start. When we did move around, the tour felt very rushed and there was very limited time to see the interesting parts of the museum. In hindsight I would have done this without a guide and just the skip the line tickets.

We took this trip on a very hot day, and in spite of timed tickets it was very crowded. Thanks to our excellent guide Renata, we made it round with a little space to appreciate the overload of artistic paintings, views of the Vatican and the highlight of the Sistine chapel. I had seen it before decades ago, but this time thanks to our guide I appreciated the background to the art as well as many anecdotes about the Popes, the artists and the Vatican City. We stopped inside the Basilica to cool down and had a rest in the portico, whilst our friends climbed the 500 or so steps to the top of the cupola. A memorable day if very hot.

There is only limited air conditioning within the museum and one visitor fainted on another tour. Because of the rules about covering knees and shoulders, the male members of the party were wearing long trousers for around 3 hours in 30+ degree conditions. If I come back I would recommend a cooler time of year.

The hot weather and large crowds detracted from our experience, but that was a result of the time of year we chose to visit the city and not on our tour operator. When we began the tour it was a bit confusing since our guide handed out listening devices and began walking down the street towards the Vatican without really explaining what we were going to do. The guide got better as the tour went along and was quite knowledgeable about the art and history. Going through the galleries on the way to the Sistine Chapel was fascinating. Appreciated guide’s efforts to expedite our time in lines and our exits. In the warm weather make sure to take along plenty of bottled water!

Our guide was clearly very knowledgeable and interested in the basilica in particular which was great, but it also meant that our tour lasted almost 5 hours with no sitting down and no opportunity to talk to each other. By the time we finally reached the Sistine Chapel, we just wanted to get out and have a sit down. It was a shame that our guide wasn’t a bit more aware of his audience and his timings because we had to rush through the museums due to having spent so much time going through every single statue and mosaic in the basilica. I admired the children in our group who were very bored and tired by the end but maintained their very good behaviour throughout.

We believed we would be in a large group especially as there was a lot of people waiting for the tour. (Neither of us would normally do a tour but felt we should, to gain the knowledge) However, we were split into much smaller groups. We had 10 in ours. The meeting point is tucked down a side street but once registered we went to a cafe just round the corner and waited till the agreed return time. The guide was very knowledge, spoke very good English and gave us a lot of information. Questions were asked and nothing was too much trouble. There is no break for refreshments in the tour but we took our own water. Also you are walking and standing the whole time so you must have comfy shoes. Visitors were turned away as they were inappropriately dressed. My husband wore combat shorts covering his knees and a t-shirt, I had a summer dress but again shoulders and knees were covered. Both totally acceptable with our trainers. The tour was worth every penny, well organised and we enjoyed. Worth seeing everything and this certainly covered it all.

Marco was our guide and it was a fabulous 3 hrs
The Basilica was amazing and Marcos knowledge was fascinating to us all as a group and at the same time respectful to the Vatican rules in the Sisteenth Chapel especially.
Cannot recommend these tours highly enough, we went in the Basilica 3 years ago without a guide and missed out on so much of the history behind the many statues, tombs and mosaics.
Thanks Marco for a great experience👏👏👏

Really enjoyed the tour by guide Marco. In the St. Peter's Basilica he gave useful background explanations at all things that we saw and connected it with other highlights in Rome. You learn things that are not written in any other tour guide book.

Due to time limitations it is not possible to visit the crypts or the roof, but if you would like to do that, you can return another time because entrance to the basilica is free (although the queue can be long). Everything is well understandable due to the headset that you receive at entrance of the basilica, although that the very beginning there was some frequency disturbance for a few minutes. Marco also took nice pictures for those who wanted and he answers any question that you might have.

Entry at the Vatican museums went smoothly as well, where it is possible to have a small toilet break. Also here the audio is good. Nevertheless, please be aware that it is really, really crowded. The highlights were explained and after the tour finishes one can still stay with the same ticket.

Our group was very large, around 30 people, and while you walk 20 minutes between sites the guide is speaking but you can’t hear him because of the large group. There is no skipping the line due to the masses of people at the Vatican. Thousands of people. We only spent about 15 mins inside the Vatican and then did another long walk to the Vatican museum and Sistine chapel. Again there were hordes of people. Getting through the hordes of people and finally into the chapel was just not worth it. It is just too crowded to enjoy it. And the. It takes another 25 minutes just to exit the building. I can only say to try to visit in the off season. It was crazy.

We found the guide to be very kind and she had a lot of knowledge. She was also very passionate, and cleary experienced in guiding. Would reccomend using a guide for the sistine chapel, but for St Peters basilica we did not really find it to be helpful as you don´t "skip" any lines but have to wait the the entire guiding group for security.

The basilica was the definitely the highlight but you don't get to skip the line here so we waited an hour in the heat and it was pretty miserable. Once inside it was great. The Vatican museums and sistine chapel did have a skip the line, but once inside we waited in line for headsets and tickets, another 30 minutes. Overall the visits were great, but the cost of the skip the line tour wasn't quite worth it. Our guide did a great job telling us stories about the sights we saw. That part was worth the money.

Summary: If you are decently independent and can follow Google Maps, there’s no need for this tour. I learned a few things about St. Peter’s Basilica but would have preferred to just do the audio guide at the Vatican Museum at my own pace.
Details: I booked this tour to try and get the most out of the Vatican and learn a few things. The meeting point was exact, I just copied the address on the confirmation into Google maps and we were able to walk from our hotel. They ask you get there 20 minutes early and that is a must! They have several different tour groups meeting at the same place and time and only one person checking everyone in. Our tour guide was Norman. He is very knowledgeable about anything and everything Italy. We started at St. Peter’s. He reminded us that since the Basilica is free, we cannot skip the line. We waited in line for about 20 minutes. We had a bathroom stop before entering the Basilica. You go through a metal detector before entering the Basilica and FFP2 or N95 masks are mandatory. Norman had a lot of information to give so we didn’t actually enter the Basilica for another 40 minutes or so. Once we finally got inside, there is no freedom to explore at your own pace, all is guided, mostly from the middle of the Basilica. From exiting the Basilica to when we got to the Vatican Museum, was another hour. Slow walking and lots of stops for people to catch up and for Norman to give information and people asking questions. It was actually difficult to walk that slow and especially in the heat (80° F). The walk is mostly flat and Google Maps says you can get there in 11 minutes on foot… You need FFP2 or N95 masks and proof of Covid Vaccination to enter the museum. You also go through a metal detector for security to get inside. We had a bathroom break inside the Vatican Museum while Norman retrieved our head sets. Once inside the Vatican Museum, the tour picked up pace significantly. We barely stopped and breezed through the rooms. On this tour, you only see a small fraction of the Vatican Museum. You are free to explore the Sistine Chapel at your leisure after the tour. The Sistine Capel is part of the Vatican Museum. The tour ended up being about 4 hours total.

It was an amazing experience, the tour guide took us to the main highlights of the area and was very informative. Would recommend this as when we got to the Vatican there was a massive queue that we got to skip, otherwise we could have easily been waiting hours for entry. There were a couple of people with limited mobility on our tour and the guide was very good and made a conscious effort to make sure they weren't left behind at any point. This was an overall brilliant experience and I highly recommend it to people visiting Rome

The tour was fine, it took us to the places it said it would and our guides gave us some information which was interesting. We are not religious in any way and are really more interested in history and architecture - obviously this is going to be quite religion focussed! But I anticipated maybe more real life history around the places e.g. how and why did Vatican City become a city?
The Vatican museums part of the tour was VERY art heavy! And I found that going around in a big group in such a cramped space with so many other tourists was really challenging.
The queue jump aspect only applies to the museums, you still have to queue for the basilica, and actually the queue for the museums was quite short so I don’t think we really saved much time there. I guess the positive is that you can hear about some of the background whilst you wait.
So it was ok, but I think this was expensive for what we got and if I could go back, I’d have done it all independently and googled the info.

First of all, our tour guide Lucia was great. She really knew her stuff. I don't know how but, she remembered everyone's name! Booking online and finding our meeting point was easy. They also reached out via email and text the day before to remind us of everything we needed to enter the Vatican. The reason I didn't give my rating a 5 is because it's a "skip the line tour". We had to wait in the same line as everyone else to get into St Peter's Basilica. (Not the tour companies rule, A Vatican rule) From the start of the tour until we got inside St Peter's was at least 1 hour. (Again, everyone has to wait in this line so it doesn't matter who you book with) After St Peter's we had to leave and walk around the outside wall to go back into the Vatican museum. We did skip the main line but it was still quite a process that took at least another 30 min. Once inside it was so packed with people that it was hard to stop and see things. Lucia was very good at stopping at important pieces of art and explaining though. She is very knowledgeable. My 4 out of 5 rating is for the tour company and guide. I don't see how any other tour company could do anything any better. The issues were with how the Vatican is running things IMO.

People are always drawn in by a negative headline trying to find something bad. Now that you're here, my wife and I thought this was a magnificent tour. Everything was pre-coordinated for all 3 venues: St. Peter's Bascilica, the Vatican Museum, and the Sistine Chapel.

Meet up location address is accurate, however, it gets a bit crowded in that active alley, so arrive early to get checked in.

You get to skip the lines, but that doesn't mean security check points unfortunately. In the heat, I was still thankful the guide could expedite everything while giving more information than I can remember 🤣

The museum entry is not just for the tour, you can continue after if you'd like. Everything was so well coordinated and pretty smooth.

All the cons about this tour are due to the Vatican and their substandard audio equipment. Our tour, Giuliano, was able to handle technical difficulties, an ill tour participant, and even assisted a lady in a wheel chair that wasn't part of the tour.

Thanks for the tour and information, Giuliano! Grazie.

These advance purchase tickets are DEFINITELY worth the purchase! You will save yourself at least 30 minutes to an hour of waiting in line to either buy the tickets or for security. With this tour you get to bypass all of those lines and people waiting, which is awesome. Our tour guide, Marco was funny, kind, and incredibly knowledgeable about the Vatican and all of the artifacts inside. I have actually been to the Vatican once before and he shared many new and interesting facts that I did not know before! Overall, it was a great value and I would highly recommend these tickets if you plan to see the Vatican, Sistine Chapel, or St Peter's Basilica.

I would 100% recommend this trip. Our guide Robert has over 20yrs experience. There isn't much he didn't know. We booked an early trip @9am. I recommend this early time as it wasn't too busy and you could easily move around the Basilica. As we moved over to the Vaccine museums & Sistine Chapel it was getting busier. Guide is so required as I wouldn't know what was the most important items to pick out

There is something to be said for 'skipping the line' I suppose, but there was no skipping the line for security and I'm not sure how much time, if any, we actually saved by skipping any lines. The tour itself was basically a fairly knowledgeable guide skimming the highlights through a radio set. It felt a little rushed, like "we have to be in this particular spot in 7 minutes so let's go!" type of feel. My wife and I both were pretty ambivalent about the quality of the tour. In fact, after it was done we ate lunch in the museum (the food was not that bad), we popped on the Rick Steve's free audio tour and did the museum again. Surprise! Rick Steve's tour stopped at the exact same places as our guide and gave out nearly identical information. But the quality of the downloaded tour was actually better than the live tour. Of course, you can't ask questions on a downloaded tour, but neither could you really ask much on the fast walk through the Basilica/Museum.

There was a lot to see on this tour and our guide, Gabriel, was very informative. The tour was non stop and you don't get many chances for respite due to the fact of trying to cram as much as possible into the 3 hour tour.
Got very busy in the Sistine Chapel but was very hypnotic looking at the paintings as the seemed to have a 3D effect when looking up. Some families with young kids struggled to finish the tour as it was full on but was definitely worth ticking of the list of things to do.

We did the tour starting at 9am-1pm, check in process easy and they have a bathroom that you can use. The tour itself was not good due to the group size. It was hard to see what the guide was pointing at, headphones would get static as tour guide too far away. I wish I either toured it myself or did a small group tour. I wish there was more information about the building and design process. Overall, I wish I did a different tour with a smaller group, not worth saving money for a large group as the entire time I was wishing it would be over.

Julian, our experienced and knowledgable guide smoothed the way though the crowd into the Vatican Museum, took great trouble to ensure we were kept informed of each step of the process and filled us in on essential historical details in a clear and friendly way. Julian was also alert to the opportunity to add the Basilica at the end of the tour when it reopened earlier than scheduled, so providing the icing on the cake. He supplied information on the difference between Roman and Neapolitan pizza to whet our appetites for a late lunch after our visit. Thanks to Julian and the team at Made in Rome Tours for a great experience from start to finish.

Worst tour and tour guide ever. We would never recommend this tour to anyone. The tour was 2+ hours late. Giovanni, our tour guide, struggled through our tour and was poorly organized and struggled to communicate with us in English. We spent huge amounts of time waiting for him to check in or checkout audio guides. He didn’t allow a family with an infant to use their stroller at different points. Our ear pieces didn’t work and several families left the tour early. Whenever we asked questions, Giovanni was defensive or failed to answer the question.

Marco is the best tour guide we have ever come across. We do a lot of tours & genuinely think Marco has a real talent for making history come alive through his knowledge & passion for the subject. He kept control of a large group in a busy environment whilst delivering an entertaining & informative tour.

The guide was terrible! He never knew how many were in our group & he would walk a half a mile without ever looking back to see if we were all still with him. He spoke quietly so no one in the back could hear him. He didn’t carry anything to help us find him like the other tours do. He also spoke very quickly which made it tough to determine what he was saying with his accent. He would skip important sites if the crowd was too big there. It was miserable. Thankfully the other participants were fun to be around or we would have left mid-way through.

This is NOT a Skip-the-Line group tour. There is no such thing apparently, when the tour guide states every soul has to wait in line when entering a house of God & you still had to queue to get in the museums. May explain the 9.00am start, in beating the crowds. 23 in this group, only had headsets for Vatican & museum, so very hard to hear what the tour guide was saying, but, when you could hear with the headsets on, the tour guide was very informative & knowledgeable & answered all questions.

This was a fantastic tour. First of all Lucia was an exceptional guide. Her knowledge and delivery of fascinating facts was a real pleasure. It was all well organised and even a courtesy text the day before helped to provide additional info like mask wearing etc.
The other thing which I thought was great was the audio. Our guide could talk quietly in the basilica and we could follow behind her at a distance listening without the need to huddle next to her.
I would absolutely recommend you take this tour, it’s a great way to experience some of the most amazing places in the world.

Guide was knowledgeable and interesting. During the parts of the tour when we were not using headsets, his voice was a bit too soft. Fascinating tour. Be aware that due to Vatican procedures in place at this time, you will still have to wait in line for entry no matter what tour you are on. It was a busy day and took just under an hour to get through security and enter. Be sure to bring a water bottle (you can refill it at multiple locations) and expect to walk about 3 miles and climb many steps on this tour. You can choose to spend as much time as you want in the Vatican Museum and Sistine Chapel at the end of the tour.

The tour was very good and very informative. I thought that the guide did the best job she could do. There were too many people in the museum, which made it less enjoyable and took time away from the tour, but this really is the best way to see as much as possible and know what you are looking at. By the time we got to the Basilica, we were on information- overload, but it was a good experience overall.

Our guide was very boring and difficult to understand. He did not have a flag so in the midst of all the crowds it was very easy to lose him. He did not wait for anyone and rushed off throughout the whole tour. Almost everyone in our group got lost at one point or another. He never made sure to make sure that everyone in his group was with him before he started talking about a certain item. It’s as if he was giving a tour to one person who is right next to him. We never had time to take pictures of our family or else we would have to run and catch up to the group.

my two boys and I just completed a tour of the Vatican City including the Sistene Chapel. we used a company called, “I ❤️ Rome”. What a brilliant experience. Alessia was our guide. Totally organised and professional, her knowledge was enhanced by her ability to knit all the facts into a coherent story that kept us engaged for the full period if the tour. Excellent experience and fully recommed. Chris, Indie and Jake from Perth Western Australia.

This was a high anxiety tour from start to finish! Our guide walked so fast & was so unorganized, and shame on Vatican Museum for allowing so many people in. We were shuffled through the museums like herds of cattle, shoulder to shoulder with little ability to enjoy the art. The Sistene Chapel was as loud as a football game when it should have been silent. We rushed to the Basilica & our guide ran through without taking time to enjoy. He was knowledgeable but the chaos totally took away from our experience. It was so unfortunate because it was a bucket list visit that was poorly executed.

Booking ahead was well worth it however the guide that day was skittish and all over the place. Running everywhere and looking disorganised. She spoke so fast that with her accent I could not understand ( I am bilingual in French and English) what she was saying let alone translate to my mum in French after. She also left us at the chapel saying we did not need her to visit it.Perhaps someone should remind her that we paid for her knowledge on top of getting us easily in the monument. She only started her tour once inside while many had started while in the queue. I know it is an express visit but a few minutes in the Basilica would have been appreciated to take it all in as we were not able to come back in due to the queues. Sorry but my mum and I both felt a bit disappointed that day.
On the flip side the booking and download of the tickets was effortless. The ear pieces and really good and clear.

The tour was very interesting and the guide was very knowledgeable. She took the time to go over fascinating stories about the people painted on the Sistine Chapel. She took the time to answer all of our questions. It's obvious that she really enjoys her job. The original meeting place is a little out of the way and hard to find.

Very well organized operation. Everything ran smoothly and on time. Our tour guide was Norman. To say he was fantastic is an understatement. His guidance through the complete zoo that is the Vatican made the whole experience quite enjoyable. It easily could have been an exercise in frustration as the crowds are overwhelming, but Norman led us through the chaos and took great care to make us feel comfortable and made our visit a very personal experience. His commentary was informative, enlightening and at times very humorous. He is simply the best! Highly recommend.

When we met the tour guide even though I had your messages with reference numbers displayed they couldn't find my details. This happened twice, with the Vatican tour on the 7th May and today, 9th, at the Colosseum. Both times we thought we were not going to be accepted but thankfully somehow they sorted it. Both tours were excellent, Lucia at the Vatican and Judy at the Colosseum were very knowledgeable and approachable.

The guide was amazing, told very interesting stories. The entire tour went by very quickly, so there was not enough time to concentrate and look at each object of the museum. Sistine Chapel and Peter's Basilica were of unique beauty

This was, no exaggeration, the best tour we went on while in Rome. It was also the most expensive, but well worth the money.

Firstly, the tour operators showed their professionalism before we even booked the tour, when they replied to a question we had (whether the tour actually includes St. Peter's Basilica; we'd seen elsewhere that it may have been closed due to Covid, which thankfully wasn't the case, as we wanted the tour to include all 3 key Vatican locations) quickly and explained everything we needed to know. They also sent us a message, in both email and SMS form, with some relevant information the night before the tour.

Secondly, the tour itself was by far the most memorable out of the 4 we went on (the other 3 obviously weren't Vatican tours so this may be like comparing apples to oranges, but the fact remains) in Rome. Marco was a delightful tour guide, he made the tour interesting, engaging and funny, and we almost never felt the 3- 3,5 hour length of the tour. We also kept a steady pace throughout, with only a bit of hurrying between the Basilica and the Vatican Museums.

We came out of the tour feeling like we've learned plenty, and much of the information extended to the rest of our stay, like being able to recognize some of the symbolism and family crests in other places throughout Rome. We really can't recommend it enough, it was one of the highlights of our trip.

The tour to the Vatican, Sistine Chapel & St. Peter's Basilica was awesome! It started out a huge group that was broke down into smaller groups at the meeting area. Our tour guide Laura, who is from Rome, was wonderful and you could tell she had a passion for the knowledge and history of the city. Highly recommend this tour and well worth the price. (On holiday from Houston, Texas)

I’ve been told before “don’t waste your money on a tour when you can see it all yourself.” We took a chance because I wanted skip the line access, but we got so much more!! Lucia, our guide is as AMAZING. She is a historian, so we got more than we could have asked for. You can tell she has a passion for the art and the history. The tour started in the basilica and touched the highlights. The ear pieces and amplifiers really helped - you could hear the entire time, which was great and eliminated the need for yelling. We went in early July 2022 and it was HOT. Bring a water bottle and fill up any one of many water fountain locations. After much information about the art and items in the basilica, including the Pietà and more less famous but equally stunning art, we moved the the Vatican museums. Total tour was 3 hours and it was time well spent. We didn’t even feel the need to stay after because the tour was so thorough. Well done and thank you, Lucia!

This tour was great! Our guide, Paola, was so friendly and knowledgeable about the history of the Vatican and Sistine Chapel and did an excellent job explaining it all. The Vatican was very busy the day we were there and being able to ‘skip the lines’ to get in saved us so much time. While there’s so much to see and do at The Vatican (one could literally spend all day there), this was a great way to see the highlights without feeling overwhelmed and still have time in our day for other activities during our quick 3 day stay in Rome. Would highly recommend this tour/company.

It was way too crowded. The groups were large and there were many groups. It was hard to take photos and stay with the guide. I think it would be ideal for less people to be allowed at a time, or was really truly crazy inside. I would not recommend this tour or do it again.

Skip the line tour of The Vatican was absolutely worth the investment. The check in location is very small, but we found it pretty easy walking using Google Maps. Our guide Lucia was extremely knowledgeable, spoke clearly, answered questions, and learned everyone in the group's names and where they were from which was a nice personal touch. Hearing the information given to other groups, I felt fortunate to have Lucia as a guide. The line the day we went would have been a two to three hour wait just to get to the gate so the skip the line fee was worth it. The Vatican itself was definitely worth the time and effort to stop and see.

My wife and I did this tour just 2 days ago. Here is what I have got to say.
LOOK NO FURTHER! If you want to see all these places in roughly 3-4 hours in a way where you also get to understand the history properly, I think this tour is awesome. I want to give a special shout-out to our tour guide Marco! The sheer amount of effort Marco put into delivering this tour was awesome. We were very happy with the thoroughness with which Marco narrated everything inside St. Peter's Basilica and near the Sistine Chapel. He went as far as discussing the marriage of art and politics in old days and how it panned out into these structures we were visiting today. So it was not just "Hey look at this, it was made in such and such year by such and such person" but a whole lot more. We essentially went through nearly every statue inside the beautiful Basilica and heard about its history. We were pretty sure we wouldn't have learned so much if we went on our own to these incredible places.

The tour started on time and the guide was able to get us into the Basilica before the line got big outside. He knew what he was doing. We were also handed radios and he spoke on a microphone so we didn't need to chase him to understand his narration. He also interacted with us, asked questions and provided answers. Also cracked jokes from time to time. Overall, we got a very neat experience.

I am reasonably certain that if you pick this tour, you will come out contented. If you get Marco as your tour guide, you surely should come out happy. That guy deserves a pay raise, no kidding!

I felt like a first Rome trip had to include a visit to the Vatican so booked this tour as I had 2 young children aged 10 and 9 and knowing very little about religion or art thought it the best way to ensure we all learned something and got the most out of the visit. Our meeting point was easy enough to find, Rome’s metro lines A and B easy to navigate to just about all the major sites. Our guide was Marco who spoke excellent English and kept the party of around 30 well engaged and kept the children’s attention well. Our entrance into Vatican City was easy with our skip the line access and despite it being fairly busy Marco did an excellent job of explaining the various pieces of art and buildings. He has already told us about the Sistine Chapel at our meeting point as you are not allowed to speak within and I was blown away by the spectacle, I am glad I paid to see it for me and my family. We then went to St Peters Basilica where Marco gave us more information, his pride and passion for Rome and art was evident and he remained behind to answer questions. All in an excellent tour with an excellent guide and worth the money.

Lucia was a fantastic tourguide. She was energetic, personable, knowledgeable and very thorough as she walked us through the Basilica and Vatican. Other than the time needed to satisfy Covid safety protocols, entry into the sites were quick and seamless. Lucia equiped everyone in our group with admission tickets and headsets for the tour.

My husband and I were in awe and humbled by the wonders of the Vatican, Sistine Chapel & St. Peter's Basilica. The mosaic's, paintings and frescos are all something to experience first-hand and having a tour guide help explain the intricacies of these marvelous works of art adds not only the experience, but to understanding the motivation behind the works.

Awesome tour!

C&Y

Absolutely well worth doing this tour not only do you see some amazing history you also get to skip the queue. Which is great as standing for 3 hours in a queue in the heat is not ideal. Our tour guide Ms Soloman was really good she knew her knowledge and was really good at communication which is key as it’s so busy. Really well organised.

Our guide was Valeria and she was truly exceptional. Her love and admiration for the history of the entire Vatican City was special and helped bring the tour to life. It was extremely hot outside and she even went above and beyond to find us shady spots to ease the heat struggles. We almost left Rome without seeing these sights via a skip the line tour and we’re so glad we didn’t. Highly recommend!

Marco was an intelligent, articulate and engaging guide. He is an impressive story-teller and historian and his briefing about the Sistine Chapel made the experience excellent, especially for one of my group who was touring for the second time but didn’t previously have the benefit of such important guidance. The tour company communicated arrangements clearly and in a timely manner. I was grateful to have taken this guided tour instead of a self-guided option, all the better for Marco’s expertise, humour and respectful execution.

The group tour was led well by passionate and knowledgeable guide The group was nice and small. There were no delays and the tour ran on time transitioning through each section smoothly. You came away having seen everything you wanted to and knowing lots of detail and history about the Vatican with plenty of time to wander around yourself afterwards. Lots of opportunity for photos. Late October was a good time to go as it was not too crowded. Make sure you go to the toilet before you go or at teh very start because they are few and far between.

Booked this to see the Vatican etc. it was great to skip the lines/queues but from that point on it was a bit manic.
It was difficult to hear our tour guide with the headphones and she spoke very quickly.
There was no point to stop and have a rest so you are walking/on your feet for 3 hours
The information that we could here was fine but I would recommend going on a self guided trip if you can avoid the queue

Brilliant tour! I will start by saying I’m not a religious person but I appreciate history and culture. This tour was amazing! Flavia was our tour guide and she talked us through everything within the Vatican museums, the Sistine chapel and the basilica. Her knowledge of Rome is brilliant and she had recommendations for anything we asked about.
It was just under 3 hours for this trip and even for skipping the line it was worth it. What makes it amazing is the service and the knowledge that is shared.
There is time for a toilet break and at no point did I feel rushed or feel that I couldn’t ask questions. Wear comfortable shoes and accept there will be crowds. They want to be there for the same reason you do!
I would highly recommend this trip!

Really brilliant tour. Definitely best to book because the queues outside were really long. Our tour guide, Amil, was brilliant. She was incredibly knowledgeable and took all kinds of questions. She covered academics, history, details of much of the artwork but it was all done in a fascinating way full of humour. The tour goes through rooms in the Vatican leading to the Sistine chapel (you aren’t allowed to talk inside so the guide explains everything in advance which great). The tour then moved via a special route for guided groups to St Peter’s Basilica where it concludes. If you do the English tour in the morning don’t book another tour afterwards because once the tour ends you can spend more time wandering around the Basilica. Amil explained that we could go down in the crypt (free) or climb into the dome (10 euros to take lift before climbing the rest on foot). Definitely do this- there’s a cafe up on the roof with great views.

This was an excellent tour and we appreciated the messages with details of the day before hand! Myself and my partner were very impressed with the organisation and friendliness of the staff when we arrived at the meeting point. On the tour, we had the pleasure of Norman who immediately made the group at ease and was great in getting the group engaged right from the start. Norman was a fantastic tour guide throughout and was highly informed and encouraged questions. At each stopping point, he talked with passion and interest and was highly entertaining as well as informative.
This is a must in Rome!

Our guide, I think his name was Marco, is phenomenal. He was awesome with our kiddos and was very knowledgeable. He was the best guide we’ve had in Rome. The reason I downgraded to 3 stars was because the Vatican was really exhausting to wander through. It was super crowded and every time you followed an exit sign you just found another corridor, pizza restaurant or bookshop. It kind of felt like the hotel California. You can check in but you can’t check out haha. The art was nice though. The Sistine chapel was beautiful. I wish I would have stopped in there longer to rest and just observe. However you are not allowed to talk in there and my kiddos are not quiet lol.

This tour was incredible. Marco was the BEST. We went straight away to the Basilica and we were one of the first groups to go in, with a totally empty Vatican piazza. We looked behind us and the people started pouring in. We were able to skip all the craziness. He was knowledgeable and passionate talking about the art and sculptures which can get a little boring with the wrong guide. This was definitely a highlights tour. We were able to stay in the Vatican museum after the tour and roam to our liking which was fantastic because there is SO much to see. 10/10 would recommend. Never wait on a line for this stuff it’s worth the money.

This was the highlight of my family's visit to Rome! The tour company is professional and keeps groups to a good size. At the Vatican and St. Peter's we were given head sets to hear our tour guide easily. We had an excellent tour guide who was well versed in the history, culture, and additional information about the Vatican, Sistine Chapel, and St. Peter's Basilica. The tour lasts several hours and it is packed with information and sights, but we didn't feel rushed. After our tour, our guide gave great lunch/gelato recommendations as well! Highly recommend!

Norman was a great knowledgeable and hilarious tour guide. My partner and I enjoyed the vatican very much. There's not much you can do about the new rules so we weren't able to skip the line (covid restrictions- so dont yell at your guides) but Norman kept it light hearted as we waited and gave us an overview before we entered. He broke down instructions so everything was easy to follow to ensure the quietest smoothest entry. We enjoyed the vatican so much that he was able to get us back in to go to the gift shop without waiting in the line which we appreciated after seeing the Sistine chapel be mindful if uou do this you will have to miss out walking around the museum on your own. For us it was worth it because we got to spend more time and see the parts of the vatican we didn't as things opened up after all the major tours had finished. We were very privileged.

Highly recommend getting Holy water :) makes a good gift for family and friends.

Overall, the places are breathtaking and even better with a knowledgeable and insightful guide. Even better if you get Norman he was actually hilarious and good to distract you if your standing in the sun goes quicker so you don't feel a thing

This tour was an amazing experience for my family of 5. Norman was our tour guide and he was very informative about the history of the catholic church. He made sure everyone was comfortable and could hear him. There was no rush in the tour. He explained the entire process of how the tour was gonna happen step by step.
St. Peter's was the first stop and then proceeded to the Vatican museum and Sistine chapel. The was an option to go back to the museum for those who wanted to see more. St. Peter's, in my option is a must see. The beauty is indescribable and I was mesmerized. Although it was a group of 30 people, Norman took his time and was patient.

Found this guided Vatican tour on TA in January before heading to Rome in early February. I normally hate the idea of being part of a ‘paddle board’ led tourist group but given the scale and breadth of what you can see, for an amateur like me on a first visit to Rome and it’s sights, a guided tour seemed like an essential piece.

No problem finding the starting location. In a group of about 20 people from all nationalities but our guide Guillian made all welcome.

Pre corovirus the skipping the lines aspect appealed and it really worked and saved a huge amount of unproductive queue time.

I’m not going to spend time on the attractions themselves since there is so much there that a few hours and fleeting looks can’t possibly do justice to.

The tour provided ‘Vatican’ headsets (pleased to see the Catholic Church continues to master its centuries old experience of money making ) and these enabled Guillian to communicate with us well. All worked and he was excellent - clearly knew the subjects and points of interest well. All the tours have to work and follow a pretty prescribed time and route and you need to be aware of this. The tour gives you a taster and if a particular part/piece attracts your interest you can return to spend more specific time at your choosing on a later date.

We had 20mins in the Sistine Chapel which is breathtaking and then the tour cheers concluded outside St Marks. We carried on independently to view the Bascillica which is stunning. I’d recommend going down to the crypt where you can see the remarkable tombs of the previous popes.

Both my partner and I would really recommend this experience and hope that the team will stay together and be able to carry on post Corona...

This tour could be great, and I’m sure many who take this have a great experience, but we just had the worst guide Ever!!

I don’t know her name, I don’t recall if she introduced herself, I do remember seeing her with a badge before the tour started and thinking to myself, I hope she’s not our guide. She’s an old lady who can barely walk, she didn’t want to be there, it was very visible on her face. She can barely speak English. She kept struggling to find the words she wanted to say.

First, it’s important to note, you don’t get to tour the Vatican itself. Only the Vatican museum.
Tour starts out at St. Peter’s square and basilica.
There is so much to see there and just not enough time. Our tour guide just kept rushing it.
Then you go to the Vatican museum, again, there is so much to see but our guide just kept rushing us.
Then you go to the Sistine chapel, again she kept rushing us all the way to the chapel.
I mentioned she could barely walk, but somehow she was flying, forcing herself through the crowds and kept saying on the radio we should keep up.

This should really be a 4-5 hour tour, the company should have better guides, and then it could be a good tour to consider. Until then, it’s a waste of time and money.

This tour was fantastic, our tour guide Giuliano was superb! So knowledgeable and really made the tour so enjoyable. The tour was around 3 hours long, with the opportunity to stay in the museum for longer once it was over. I definitely wouldn’t have learnt or enjoyed this as much without a tour guide who knew the history and small stories to accompany everything you got to see. 5 stars.

Skipping the line was NECESSARY. Having someone walk us through the museums wasn’t necessary but it was nice to have someone to fill in the story behind everything as opposed to figuring it out on our own. Well worth the money for this experience. Highly recommend seeing the Vatican this way.

Giovanni was wonderful, patient and taught us so much. Learned about the art history of sculpting hands, feet and torsos. The history of Italy and the creation of Vatican City. The ceiling of the chapel was iridescent - especially when you hear the stories behind the creation.

Lucea was good controlling a group of 14 I think, skipping lots of queues and taking 2.5 hours to do the entire tour. Enthusiastic and knowledgeable but so much info to take in and maybe too fast talking at times. Basilca and Sistine very good.

I would suggest that unless you are well versed in Vatican history a guide is essential for these visits. The tour was very well organised and our guide very knowledgeable. The communication prior to the tour, where to arrive, times what to expect etc was excellent. It was the best tour I have been on, however, the only slight downside for me was the Vatican museum was very crowded so sometimes difficult to see everything, but that would be the same for everyone. Highly recommended

In my mind, what makes a great tour, is the guide. If you’re fortunate enough to get Giuliano, this tour hits it out of the park.

Even without Giuliano, this tour is a winner as it efficiently covers St Peter’s, the museum and the Sistine chapel in approximately 3 1/2 hours. It hits the high points of all three with time allocated appropriately. We dragged ourselves out of bed for the 9am tour and it was worth it. Even though December is off-season (not to mention Covid), the later lines, while manageable, were longer. We were told that approximately 8-10 million people usually visit the Vatican in a normal year. 2020 saw that number drop by 80%. This was our first trip, so we were not sure what to expect about crowd sizes. We have been delighted to find the crowds are here, but they’re smaller and less oppressive. December is a great time to come to Rome and I higher recommend this tour!

Overall this was a good tour. We really enjoyed the Basilica and our guide was very knowledgeable. The Vatican museum was so crowded I don’t even really remember much of that part and would probably skip that next time. The Sistine chapel was beautiful.

Well organised logistics in utter chaos. The agency seemed to have good control with a big group of tourists. Guide Paola was swift and efficient (sometimes maybe a bit too efficient, although maybe difficult to avoid in the total mayhem of the Vaticane Museums). Paola was knowledgeable but the headphones at the museum were of poor quality and it was sometimes difficult to hear way she said.
Still; all in all an ok way to see the Vatican; it is worth paying for the guide and the past-the-queue pass. Note; the earlier you book the lower the price.

We wanted something speedy, and that's what we got, so no complaints there! Our guide, Germana, was very kind, but didn't seem to be very knowledgeable throughout the tour (with lots of communication issues) and forgot the floors we were meant to be on, kept doubling back because she'd forgotten to tell us something important about what we were seeing, and/or correcting a mistake she'd made about a piece of art, etc. It was pretty scattered and not very organized, and while she made a point multiple times of telling us not to speak in the Sistine Chapel, she gathered us around after a few minutes and started explaining things to the point where the guards had to shush her...so she lowered her voice and continued. So odd! Like I said, she was a very nice person and probably doing her best, but she was not an adequate guide in our opinion. She did, however, try her best to accommodate the tourist in the motorized scooter who was part of our group, for which I commend her.

Me and my family did this tour this week. Lucia was our guide she was amazing very knowledgable and made this experience so worth while. Good value for money with skip the line
I would recommend this my teenage children enjoyed as much as we did
Thankyou Lucia

Highly recommended. We had a scheduling problem and the staff could not have been more accommodating. The tour guide whisked us past the long line waiting to get in and helped us to weave through the large crowds. The detailed information he provided gave great insight into the history and beauty which surrounded us. He showed us where he was baptized and married in a chapel at the Vatican. Talk about having a long term connection! Everything was great.
Side comment: A store a few doors down from their office sells everything for the well dressed priest. Worth a look.

The Vatican, including St. Peter's and the Sistine Chapel was seriously crowded to the point that we lost all sense of it being a spiritual pilgrimage. Our guide was decent, and not responsible for the crowds and heat, but overall this was not nearly as enjoyable of a trip as we had hoped. We had to rush through and past amazing works of art, and there were few uncrowded places to breathe and no way to exit without walking through in an "industrialized tourism" sort of way.

An informative and fascinating tour of the Vatican Museum, Sistine Chapel & St Peters.

Our guide was (as you would hope) incredibly knowledgeable. He was an expert in marble which was fascinating, as he pointed out some pieces that you would ordinarily miss.

The tour was full of incredible information and facts that you wouldn’t get on your own.

Our group was a good size and the guides gave us plenty of time to look at everything we needed to, it didn’t feel rushed.

This place is VERY busy, you need to expect crowds, but this didn’t detract from our experience at all.

Our guide left us at St Peters so we had as much time as we needed to explore this incredible church.

I was with 2 teens, who really enjoyed the experience, it was well worth it!

This is one of the most important tours to take, please do it! MARCOS was an exceptional guide who knew the history of the Vatican by heart. Marcos made us feel at home while explaining the St Peter’s basilica, the Vatican museums and the Sistine chapel. He knew every single detail and dedicated the time to make sure everyone was enjoying the time and learning. This tour should always be done by people like him who have a deep knowledge and understanding of our Catholic faith. I strongly suggest this particular tour. We had to do no lines. Amazing.

This was hands down our best tour of a 10 day trip to Italy. Our tour guide Marco combined knowledge, humor, excellent English to captivate adults and children alike. Thank you so much for an unforgettable visit!

THE GOOD was meeting interesting people within our group, seeing La Pieta which is one of my favorite statues in the world and seeing the majesty of St Peters Basilica.
THE BAD was that it was extremely crowded to where they had to cordon off a hallway and open another to make the waiting line longer. It reminded me of the lines I've seen in Disney World. THE UGLY was that our tour guide was speed walking with us everywhere. At one point we had to sprint to keep up with him (and I'm a marathoner). It made for a bad experience and not how a tour of a unique place like this should have been run. OVERALL I would skip this tour company and find one that actually cares about the experience.

The Vatican tour with Giuliano has been the best one we’ve had in a long time. Giuliano has the extraordinary capacity of recreating the atmosphere of ancient times, of integrating the information in the whole,of graduating the sequence of masterpieces, while being extremely knowledgeable and humorous at the same time.
I would definitely recommend his guidance to all tourists coming to Rome

It is no chance that this is one of the highest-rated guided tours to the Vatican, Sistine Chapel & St. Peter's Basilica. I would definitely book again if I had the chance!

Giuliano (our tour guide) did an excellent job at explaining to us the history behind all of the places that we visited, and he did with such a charisma that made the well worth 3-hour tour all the more enjoyable. While 3 hours might seem like a lot, but the time went flying at his guidance and I never had the feeling that the tour might have been too long. Quite the opposite, I wish we had more time to see other rooms of the Vatican Museum!

My only "complain" is that on the guided tour to the Vatican museum, we didn't go to one of the most famous rooms (the Raffael Rooms).
