If you are considering seeing the Vatican Museums, the Sistine Chapel and St Peter’s Basilica the I suggest this is the only way to do it.

This is one of the best trips we have been on. Skip the line is the best thing you can do and with a guide.
Our guide Juiliono was just fantastic and so informative and how he kept an eye on all of us I will never know as we were a group of 30 plus but he did. He always made sure we were all good. My fav part was saint peters basilica. You would have to see it to get the proper feelings we got. So I won’t spoil it but it’s worth every penny.

Firstly, we chose the best tour of these historical landmarks. Our tour guide, Guiliano, introduced himself to all of us and gave us an excellent introduction to the monuments. At selected areas, he stopped and gave us an overview of the artworks and buildings, giving these a historical context as well as providing background that we would have missed. With 20 000 visitors a day, he kept us all together and helped make this the best tour from our trip in Italy. Well done! We would definitely recommend spending some extra money for this tour - it is worth it!

Juliano was a fantastic tour guide! Very knowledgeable, sharing many fascinating facts about the artworks in the Vatican Museum and the Sistine Chapel. We skipped all the lines and finished tour within 3 hours! Definitely Recommend!

Giuliano was our guide and made this trip so different than the previous time we visit the Vatican Museum. Very organised, Taking care of small details, lead the group through the museum with humour yet provided a lot of information which made this tour so enjoyable and educational.
Not only we saved many hours waiting but me gained an amazing experience in the museum itself.
Highly recommended
Our guide Julian was great and he did an exceptional job of navigating the unending lines and crowds. It’s very confusing to navigate this area if you don’t have a guide.

Highly recommend this tour. We visited today and the queues were incredible. Just for being able to bypass all of that would have been worth it but Giuliano, our guide was great too. His care of the group stood out from all of the others we saw and he gave us just the right amount of information about all 3 areas. This meant that we thoroughly enjoyed our visit and are far more knowledgeable than we would have been had we tried to do it ourselves.

This was a brilliant trip and well worth it. Skipping the queue is a must, even during a less busy time you would be waiting 3 or 4 hours at least. The guide, Giuliano (please excuse spelling), is fantastic and makes everyone feel very welcome, whilst also being incredibly knowledgable. We personally got a lot out of it.

The museum did feel like a little bit of a canter through, but you get all the keys things shown to you and explained well. Then in the main attraction the Sistine Chapel, you get bags of time to soak in a truly spectacular site. Plus, with all the background knowledge from the guide to search for it makes it even more interesting.

Worth noting the Dome is not included and will cost you and extra €10 each to go up the lift and then walk the remaining 300+ steps (you can take all 500+ steps for €8 each, but i would pay the extra). However, it is also well worth it.

We had a wonderful Vatican tour experience with Giuliano (tour guide).

We set out this morning on a sunny Italian day with a visit to the Vatican - starting at the Vatican Museum (where many of Michelangelo sculpting works are housed); followed by a 15 minute stay in the Sistine Chapel admiring all the art works that surround the Chapel; then a walk through the very opulent St Peter's Basilica in the Vatican. Thousands of visitors were spread throughout the Vatican all day - it is a "tourist" hot spot for anyone interested in history and art.
Juliano was a great guide. Very informative and great at ensuring we didn’t get lost as it was incredibly busy. So glad we booked as the queues were extremely long.

What a brilliant tour and a brilliant tour guide - Guiliano! The tour started in the old street of the Borgo Pio with Guiliano expalining the paintings in the Sistine chapel - because, of course, there (supposed to be) silence in side hence no way to explain once inside (Guiliano was at great pains to explain that their should be silence, however, other tours were no so observant). We then had a 20 minute walk to the Museum entrance, with Guiliano taking care to make sure everyone on the tour knew where they were going. We did indeed 'skip the line' and went straight inside to security and we were straight through. We hung around a while as, Guiliano explained, it makes sense to go to the loo right at the start of tour (obviously, this makes it easier for him, to avoid losing anyone inside, but I think also for everyone). Then, collected our ear-piece so that we can hear everything Guiliano tells us, and off at a slow pace through the museum galleries (they are packed with tourists like us, obviously!), with Guiliano providing a farily constant flow of extremly relevant, inciteful and detailed commentary of everything we saw, pointing out the more important pieces, with much detailed background info - he really knows his stuff! It would have bee nice to have some more time to look at specific pieces, but of course that is impossoible on a guided tour since everyone will have their own interest as to where to spend extra time. Also, we did not see everything in the museum - but then, we did avoid a 2-3 hour wait outside!
The Sistine chapel is astonishing (albeit, we did feel like cattle herded inside - but that's because there are just so many people wanting to see it, not a fault of the tour), and Guiliano was keen to make sure the group had a good vantage point to see all the paintings, and from two diffferent spots. After this, we headed down to St. Peter's Basilica. Guiliano did not accompany us inside, which was a shame, as I am sure he could have provided some context to the architecture, and artifacts inside what is a quite stunning church. There was no time limit on how long we stayed inside.
Overall, the tour was well worth the money, with a tour guide who not only imparted his detailed knowledge of the buildings and their contents, but also made the tour fun - we thoroughly enjoyed it and I definitely recommend it.

Tour guide, Julian was very knowledgeable and easy to understand. He hit all the important points. Also answered ALL of our questions at the end, patiently! If I had to complain about anything, it was being rushed through the museum portion. There were so many people so it was understandable. I would strongly recommend this tour!
The tour was absolutely brilliant. Giovanni explains everything in details. Five Stars for a fantastic tour guide. Giovanni was the best tour guide we had on our trip to Rome
Giuliano was so friendly & knowledgable I would highly recommend this tour! We learnt so much & having skip the line was well worth it looking at the queues for each individual part of the tour!

Firstly, a 'Skip the Line' tour is an absolute must, and so easy. When we were there the queue for people paying at the gate ran the full circle around St Peters Square and was taking 2-3 hours to get in. This tour was really easy to book, and good value for money. Local knowledge adds so much to the experience and brings things to life, and amazingly the headsets worked perfectly so we could hear everything our guide was saying. The one thing that would have improved this tour for us would have been if our guide had come into the Basilica with the group, as did other guides that we saw, even if it was only to point out the main features before leaving us to wander around. Overall though we loved it and would definitely recommend.

When I booked this tour I have to admit I was a little sceptical of the “skip the line part” as most of the tours offer the same. How can we all skip the line?? How wrong I was! The skip the line worked perfectly and is very well organised.
Guilliano was an excellent guide, providing detailed history as well as entertaining anecdotes which really added to the experience.
He also helped me with booking the Dome visit (not included in this) which I loved
Overall I went solo on this tour, so didn’t need to worry about anyone getting lost etc. However the Vatican is extremely busy and my advice would be to definitely book a tour rather than go it alone.
Highly recommended
My first time to the Vatican and it was beautiful. Definitely an experience I would recommend for anyone.

Highly recommend. Our group was 20 ppl and our guide Guiliano was amazing. He really looked after us, was extremely personable and walked backwards THE WHOLE way so he could interact with us and make eye contact. He also showed us the pictures of the Sistine chapel before we started the tour in the shade, as it was extremely hot that day and we really appreciated not standing around in the gardens. 10 out of 10, recommend to a friend!!!!

Everything was smooth and well planned from the beginning. The tour guide, Giuliano, never lost sight of his big group and explained about what we were about to see so that we don't miss anything. It was worth of every penny.

Had the best tour with Guilliano spoke very good English, was patient with us amongst all the other people visiting, was worth every dollar as we skipped the line and went straight in, he has lots of knowledge and explains everything so well, highly recommend his company

We had the pleasure of Giuliano as our Guide on this wonderful tour. The group was relatively small (about 15) and Giuliano introduced himself to us prior to starting. He immediately put everyone at ease, considered our welfare throughout (often seeking a shaded area in the hot midday sun) and his depth of knowledge must be second to none! His warm, friendly nature created a lovely atmosphere (in the very crowded Vatican and Sistine Chapel). There are lots of skip the line tours (with the size of the line today, this was the only way to visit the Vatican, Sistine Chapel and St Peter's Basilica) and I can only review this one, but it definitely felt like we received a 5 star service and would quite happily recommend this company (especially with Giuliano as the Guide) to all my family and friends visiting Rome!

Guilianno was a fantastic tour guide. We had about 15 in our group and he made sure everyone stayed together but also got the most from the tour. We didn’t queue at all. The whole experience took about 2 and a half hours. Guilianno was very knowledgable and passionate. The only disappointment was that people were not silent in the Sistine Chapel, but that was not the tour’s fault. Worth every penny.

Really enjoyed the tour , made even more interesting by our guide Guillo.Very knowledgeable and kept the group interested and together for 3 hours . Took time to welcome everybody to the tour and at the end said goodbye individually . Highly recommend the tour . The Vatican museums are amazing and sistine chapel overwhelming. St Peter's Church and Square breathtaking . Would do it all again with the same guide .

This was a great experience and worth the money!! You get to skip all the lines and admissions are included in the price. Our guide was very knowledgeable and explained things very well! This is a family run business and I’d rather pay for this rather than a huge company. Also I liked our group size.

Great tour, very enthusiastic and funny guide!

Sistine chapel was far too full and no one respected the silent policy which ruined the ambience and the experience of the chapel! However this was obviously not the tour agencies fault.

Definitely worth paying to skip the line and the tour was brilliant. There were lots of people queuing while we walked past them. The tour guide definitely is very knowledgeable.

The only slightly down side I would say is the radio reception on my headset, it's quite temperamental and as it's quite a large group, you can't always stand close to the guide.

Absolutely stunning!! The history and art is something to see if you haven’t yet been here. If you are a believer you will want to visit this place and if you are not a believer in God it may very well make you one. Why would someone ( Michelangelo) spend so much time painting the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel? Enough said.
Great and well informed guide, catered for different people. Easy walk. But jumping the long cue was the best part.

This was my first and most perfect tour in Rome, worth the money cause I didn’t have to stop and wait in the line not even for a moment, our guide Juiliano was incredible, highly knowledgeable, very professional, had an amazing smile on his face all the time from the very first moment till the end.
The pace of the tour was just perfect, not too slow and not too rushed.
Highly recommend the tour, and you will get the most unforgettable tour if you were lucky enough to have it with Juiliano.

Loved, loved, loved this tour and our fabulous guide, Guliano!!! He was very informative, energetic and was able to keep our group of about 20 people together. We started out at their office and he gave us a rundown of what to expect and showed us images/art work ahead of time in order to explain the back ground. We had individual earbuds so it was easy to hear him amongst the crowds.

Had a fabulous tour. Our guide was excellent and provided the perfect mix of knowledge and humor. It is evident he is extremely passionate about his job and we loved touring with him. Well worth the money and would highly, highly recommend this tour!
Juliano was a great guide made us all feel at ease and very knowledgeable, next time I will book it and take the kids

Our guide Giuliano did an excellent job. The whole family learned a lot and Giuliano also managed to keep our 3 kids interested in the history surrounding the Vatican/Rome. The price for the tour is very reasonable and I would highly recommended you to join this tour no matter with or without kids.

After the tour I strongly suggest you go to the top of the Basilica. This is not included in the tour, but it is worth the money and sore legs. The hardcore visitor will take the stairs all the way to the top - 551 steps - but if you pay a little extra you can take the lift and you are "only" left with 320 steps. It is tough but worth it. The view is just spectacular. Enjoy.

I purchased this tour for my husband and I. It was great! The group was small and Giuliano was a great guide, very knowledgeable. He told us what to expect and many interesting and fun facts about the Vatican and the artists.

My girlfriend and I booked with Giuliano purely by chance. We had intended to visit the Colosseum independently, but on arrive, secured a great deal for the tour, which included Palatine Hill and Roman Forum. We were so glad we did, the knowledge of the guides was exceptional and made our experience much better than it would have been doing it ourselves. For this reason we booked for the Vatican Tour the following day.

We met promptly to make our way there and despite a bit of waiting around (due to the security inside the Vatican Museum) we were on our way quickly, and avoided the massive queues outside.

Giuliano was very knowledgeable but also kept things moving at a good pace, but without rushing the group. We thoroughly enjoyed the tour, and he done everything he could to ensure we were getting enough time at each part and explaining things fully to us. So much so, that another tour guide behind us was shouting at him for not rushing through! We appreciated that and it meant we really got the most out of our day.

I would highly recommend Giuliano to anyone considering this tour and you definitely get great value for money.

Thanks for making our trip so enjoyable.

Guiliano was the perfect host - his knowledge and direction throughout the tour was 6 star. From the beginning right through to the end he was so informative and guided us through every aspect with ease.
I have never seen anyone walk backwards so much in my life.
You never know what to expect when you sign up to these tours and I have to admit I was a littele apprehensive when being led down the narrow side streets of Rome to the tour office.
Dont worry!! Giuliano was the perfect host throughout.

I wanted to like this tour but can't recommend it. Now, I'd give the tour guide 7 stars out of 5 if I could. Marco was great with the structure and schedule he had to work with. But for the price, allotted time, and crowds to contend with, the experience wasn’t as rich as expected.

St. Peter's Basilica is free entry, so you don't skip a line for it. I felt this was the best part of the tour, but it had no skip-the-line benefit. Marco’s info was good, but also info you can research on your own.

In the Museum, your tour group of ~30 people tries to stay together while mixed in with 1000s of other people in crowded halls, all jostling your way to the Sistine Chapel. Marco pointed out things along the way, but because of the crowds, I had to focus more on keeping his flag in sight than viewing art.

Once in the Chapel, the tour allots only 10 minutes before you're asked to exit together.

If I repeated the tour, I'd only try not to lose sight of the tour guide on the way to the Chapel. I would then return the radio to the guide before entering the Chapel, along with a gratuity for his or her work, then spend as long as I wanted to gaze up at the ceiling without keeping track of time. I'd also plan a couple hours afterward to take in more of the museum's works in less crowded halls and wings.

If I wanted to visit these places again, I wouldn't do a full skip-the-line tour, just look for skip-the-line access to the Museum and Chapel, then take my time to view things at my own pace.
Amazing host with a wealth of knowledge and wonderful friendly manner. I have been to Rome before and I learned so much more from Julian on this tour.
We had an amazing tour with our guide, Marco. The tour was very informative and very interesting. He was very passionate about Rome's history. I would thoroughly recommend it.
Marco was our guide and his knowledge was exceptional lovely guy learned lots and thoroughly enjoyed it great value for money

This was a tour that was well worth doing. It's very well organised. The information received was accurate. We were accompanied by Marco who is very knowledgeable and engaging. You can visit the Vatican by yourself but the guided tour makes it so much more interesting and you really get so much out of it. Afterall, you've paid to come to Rome you might as well make the most of it. Well done Marco and team. Highly recommended!

Marco was a fabulous guide.
We were fortunate to visit on quite a quiet Saturday afternoon no queuing which apparently is very unusual.
Would definitely recommend so informative listening to Marco.

Incredible tour! Our guide, Juliano, had such a great knowledge of the Vatican and all the history associated with it and delivered with such enthusiasm that made it particularly enjoyable and captivating. I’m very pleased my partner and myself did the tour as we were able to get a lot more out of the overall experience of the Vatican City.

Giuliano was an exceptional guide! We couldn't have asked for a smoother, more professional tour. His knowledge of Italy and the historical sights was very impressive. This was an unforgettable part of our trip to Rome. We're so glad we booked with Made in Rome tours, and feel very fortunate that Giuliano was our guide.

We would recommend this trip to anyone who wants a unique Vatican experience! Ciara/Claire knows all the hot spots of the museums and we could not recommend more for this tour.
Enjoy your trip in The Vatican City!
The tour is very informative. Our tour guide Marco made it very interesting and avoided the boring parts. We definitely recommend this tour!

Great guide and impressive art and history. Three hours are no where near enough, perhaps a week long tour of each of the museum and St Peters is needed!

Awesome visit

Well worth pre booking, although January quiet overall,, the knowledge and expertise from Juliana was invaluable, skipped the queues. An amazing and emotional experience definitely worth a couple of hours out of your day.

Very nice and interesting tour! Guilliano is a very very nice and very knowledgeable guide!
Easy to get lost though) I did but managed to find the group later)))

The guide was very very good! Spoke English very well and had a very in-depth knowledge of the area. He did not walk too fast and gave us time to enjoy what we were experiencing. He also answered any questions we had.
Giuliano is a very calm and knowledgeable guide. Vaticano is amazing site and Giuliano contribute to make the experience even better.
The Vatican Museum could have been an overwhelming experience but Guiliano made it enjoyable. He expertly guided us through the amazing collections and the crowds.

We did Vatican Tour and coliseum tour what an amazing 2 days we had very knowledgeable guide explaining everything

Thanks Juliano is was great highly recommend this tour company you will not go wrong

When we made the skip the line at the Museum enterance where we had to wait for a while. The tour was great! There’s just so much to see at the Vatican that you could go every day for a year and still not see it all. The ceiling of the hall of maps alone would take months to “see” fully, much less soak in and appreciate.

That’s more of an FYI for future visitors. For the tour itself, it was great. No wasted time, but still as thorough a visit as you could do in a group setting. Our guide (I’m sorry, I can’t remember his name) was great - friendly, professional and fair. I asked about the Raphael Rooms early into the tour and while it’s not part of the tour experience, he was able to keep us all together so that we made good enough time to be able to fit in a detour through the Rooms, and that may have been my favorite part.

All in all, the tour went for 3 hours and 40 minutes.

A few final FYIs for those that are planning a Vatican trip. This is all from October 2022:
- we brought proof of vaccination but we never needed to show it
- one woman in our group was asked to cover her shoulders (and she came prepared with a cardigan) but men with shorts were able to enter just fine. You may not want to risk it but I wanted to point it out just the same.
- we were in and out of the Sistine Chapel in about 5 minutes. That was a bit disappointing. It was also surprisingly noisy, even without the guards having to say “no photo!” every 10 seconds. I imagine this was just a necessity of getting a tour through the whole thing in a reasonable amount of time, but that was still a bit anticlimactic.
- Tour didn’t include any souvenir store time, and by the time we finished in St Peter’s Cathedral, we didn’t know if we could even double back to the museum store.

Overall, great tour and great visit. We took a lot of great tours on our recent trip through Paris / Rome / London, but this was a low-point.

First, the group sizes are absurdly large, and what happens with groups like this is you end up spending all your time and energy just keeping the group together and the logistics of that.

Second big one - the tour said it was 3 hours, but we ended up leaving the door mid-way through the Vatican Museum because we were on track for a 4.5+ hour experience, which is just too much and not what we were after.

Third - our guide was not a good communicator and didn't explain at each step where we were headed and what to expect in terms of walking, waits, etc. It was the same feeling you get at the airport when your flight is delayed and no one tells you anything? Not a fun vibe.

The best part of the tour was St. Peters Basilica (the first bit). This attractions is free to anyone without a ticket and everyone waits for the security line, so the tour itself doesn't skip anything here, but our guide was good at pointing out details and taking us into spots we may have missed (Crypts below for example).

But then when transitioning to the Vatican Museum, things went downhill - walk was way too long w/o any warning, place was packed so it was near impossible to stay together, the audio headsets used there (different from the tour group's units) didn't work well.

Vatican Museum is setup like an IKEA with no shortcuts- you are on a linear path through room after room of potentially interested stuff but everyone is just on a death-march to see the Sistine Chapel.

The problem is the Vatican Museum tickets sell out (presumably to the tour groups), so you have to book a tour and go through this hellish process to see the one thing on your bucket list.

And then after you see it, the Vatican Museum makes you go through another 30 minutes of gift shops, stairways, etc. just to get to the exit. Its not fun, its the IKEA from hell.

A lot of this is not the fault of the tour operator, so my recommendation is (at least in summer) go see St. Pauls on your own or with a small group, skip the Vatican Museum altogether and lit to your friends and tell them you saw the Sistine Chapel even if you didn't. You'll be happier for it.

Despite all these 'bad customer' challenges, "Giuliano" , "Carlotta" and their team never turned their back on us. They found solutions to all our issues. They found a wheelchair we could use in the Basilica and for the long walk to the Vatican museum despite only giving them hours of notice. They had a team member wait for our late arrival and quickly got us with the group. They offered to hold our thermos because they told us the Vatican would toss it.. and then a team member waited for an hour after the tour and met us with the thermos as we exited (we were shocked !). As I was checking the camping chair at the museum, Carlotta came to our rescue - asking the security team to take a 2nd look at our chair and they let us have it for the tour. Our senior mother really needed it as there is a lot of walking in the Vatican museums but not a lot of places to sit. "Carlotta" was an amazing guide. She has to be one of the most educated guides in Rome. She gave us so many details and interesting tidbits about so many items. She kept checking on us all the time, making sure we were ok.
